book.fireclay.primer.p1:
Clay remembers the fire.

Throw it, glaze it, fire it just right, and the clay keeps what the fire gave it.

This is the craft of the Fireclay Guild. Read it by the kiln.
book.fireclay.primer.p10:
The Effigy

Eight fireclay, a blaze glaze, a lined kiln held at 860–940° for forty seconds.

Fire it white and true, and it will stand guard.
book.fireclay.primer.p2:
The Wheel

Load clay balls, up to eight. Sneak with an empty hand to pick a shape: tile 1, bell 3, jar 4, urn 6, effigy 8 (fireclay only).

Five throws with an empty hand and the piece pops off.
book.fireclay.primer.p3:
The Kiln

Greenware, glaze, fuel. Heat settles where the fuel wants: wood 320°, coal 520°, coal block 620°, lava 670°, blaze 750° and up.

Fuel burns only while a piece fires.
book.fireclay.primer.p4:
The Window

Each piece cures only inside its heat window. Below it, progress waits.

Two seconds above it and the piece cracks. Keep the shards: every good potter has a pile.
book.fireclay.primer.p5:
Bellows & Damper

Face a bellows at a burning kiln: each pump adds 35°.

Redstone into the back or top opens the damper. The fire halves and the kiln cools twice as fast.
book.fireclay.primer.p6:
The Sweet Spot

The middle 40%% of the window. Hold it for nine tenths of a glazed firing and it comes out a Masterwork, signed with your name.

Chimes, vigils and ember tiles keep the shine but forget the name.
book.fireclay.primer.p7:
Comparators

A kiln reads 0 below the window, 1 to 14 inside it, 8 at its heart and 15 when too hot.

Wire it to the damper and one thermostat fits every recipe.
book.fireclay.primer.p8:
Glazes

Mix clay, water and a mineral.

Lapis remembers.
Amethyst listens.
Glow ink keeps vigil.
Blaze holds heat.
Echo holds a soul.

The kiln seals it in.
book.fireclay.primer.p9:
Fireclay

Shards become grog. Grog, clay and sand make fireclay; bake it to bricks and line the kiln.

A lined kiln reaches 1000°. Coal runs hot in it: fire tiles on wood.
